parole.testo: Reborrowing from French acrobatie < acrobate, itself from Koine Greek ἀκροβάτης (akrobátēs) from ἄκρον (ákron, “peak”) -βάτης (-bátēs, “walker”) (not from ᾰ̓κρόβασις (ăkróbasis, “support e.g. foot of table”). For figurative sense, it is a calque of French faire des acrobaties.
Semantic loan from French vecteur. From Hellenistic Koine Greek διάνυσμα. Morphologically, from δι- (δια-) (“to go through”) + άνυσμα (“vector, distance covered”).

parole.significato: to function, to operate, to work
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek λειτουργῶ (leitourgô) (contracted form of λειτουργέω (leitourgéō)) with semantic loan from French fonctionner and the ecclesiastical senses borrowed learnedly from Koine Greek.
Learned borrowing from French pornographie, itself coined from Koine Greek πορνογράφος (pornográphos). First attested in 1893. See πόρνη (pórni), πόρνος (pórnos) & -γραφία (-grafía).
